issues.legal_issue: Heirs of a cultivating tenant may satisfy the personal-cultivation requirement through physical labour contributed by a family member related by marriage, but the nature of that work must be determined before their status is decided.
material_facts: The deceased tenant's heirs were his widow and daughter, who did not themselves contribute physical labour to cultivation of the land.
The daughter's husband held a power of attorney from the heirs and was said to be working in connection with cultivation of the land.
The landlord contended that the husband's work was only supervision; the Sub-Collector made no finding about the nature of his work.
The proceedings concerned an application to deposit rent arrears on behalf of the heirs.
issues.conclusion: A son-in-law can be a member of the heirs' family, so his physical labour in cultivating the land could satisfy the personal-cultivation requirement for the heirs. Because the nature of his work was not found, the Court set aside the orders below and remitted the matter for a determination of whether he contributed physical labour.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(a) and 2(ee) of the Madras Cultivating Tenants Protection Act, 1955, a cultivating tenant must carry on personal cultivation, which includes contributing the physical labour of a family member. Family is not confined to a Hindu joint family and may include a relative by marriage, such as a son-in-law. In Abubucker Lebbai v. Zamindar of Ettayapuram, the Madras High Court held that supervision is not physical labour, a view this Court approved; the broader view in Kunchitapatham Pillai v. Ranganatham Pillai was considered too wide. Since no finding established what work the son-in-law performed, the Court directed a factual determination on remand.

rule.if: rent_arrears_deposit_proceeding and claimants_are_heirs_of_a_tenant and claimants_do_not_personally_contribute_physical_labour and family_member_is_related_by_marriage and family_member_work_is_claimed_but_its_nature_is_unresolved

predicates.rent_arrears_deposit_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a request to deposit rent arrears on behalf of persons claiming a tenant's protection.
predicates.claimants_are_heirs_of_a_tenant: The persons seeking protection inherited their status from a tenant.
predicates.claimants_do_not_personally_contribute_p: The claimant heirs do not themselves perform physical labour in cultivating the land.
predicates.family_member_is_related_by_marriage: A person related to the claimant heirs by marriage is involved in work connected with cultivation.
predicates.family_member_work_is_claimed_but_its_na: It is claimed that the family member works in connection with cultivation, but the lower forum has not determined whether that work involves physical labour.

issues.definition: When heirs who do not themselves perform physical labour rely on claimed cultivation work by a family member related by marriage, and the nature of that work remains unresolved, the orders are set aside and the matter is sent back for a finding on physical labour.
